source.title: There is a Singularity in the Loss Landscape

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains AlexNet and VGG-16 on CIFAR-10 and measures curvature, gradient projections, and training-loss changes to test aspects of V5. It does not report the training-error outcomes named in V1–V4 or V6.
record.gate_note: Rows record the study’s own measurements of edge-of-stability ratios, gradient projections, and loss changes. Dataset sizes and cusp plots are not rows for these versions because they do not measure the training-error behavior they name. Cited findings from other papers are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study independently measures Hessian eigenvalues relative to 2/η during full-batch gradient descent, directly testing V5's edge-of-stability component with the same basic method and measure as Cohen et al. It extends the analysis to multiple eigenvectors and projected gradient steps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the author's conclusion: increasing dataset size produces a limiting singularity near which training proceeds, causing top-subspace edge-of-stability behavior and gradient concentration, while most subsequent learning comes from the bulk component. The singularity and causal explanation are the author's interpretation of finite experiments; Section 5.4 explicitly acknowledges that finite networks with bounded weights and finite datasets have finite gradients and curvature.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments use non-stochastic gradient descent without momentum on CIFAR-10, measure Hessian eigenvalue-based stability ratios and loss changes from gradient projections, and do not test the version’s squared-loss wide-network or extended full-batch sharpness recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The edge-of-stability ratio varies with learning rate: at η=0.0001, ρ10 stays below 0.246 while ρ9 reaches at least 0.693. The text reports that tanh networks at η=0.003 failed to converge and excludes them from analyses; VGG-16-tanh at η=0.0001 converged too quickly for more than two analyses.

fits_no_version.finding: Bulk curvature remains well below the stability threshold at the lowest learning rate, separating it from the top eigenspace.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: During these full-batch CIFAR-10 runs, edge-of-stability behavior is concentrated in the top nc−1 Hessian eigendirections.

fits_no_version.finding: At selected edge-of-stability checkpoints, isolated top-projection steps increase loss or change it little, whereas isolated bulk-projection steps consistently decrease it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At these checkpoints, the bulk gradient component supplies loss-reducing directions despite the gradient's concentration in the top subspace.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient components grow abruptly at the same iteration their eigendirections enter the edge of stability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Entry into the edge of stability coincides with gradient concentration in the top Hessian subspace.

fits_no_version.finding: Adaptive low-step-size experiments show dataset-dependent peak curvature and increasingly cusp-like loss cross-sections.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing dataset size produces sharper local loss geometry near the training trajectory, which the author interprets as evidence of a limiting singularity.

record.code_released: not stated (the paper says code will be released)
record.problems: No controls are described. Experiments use one dataset, CIFAR-10; the main series uses two architectures and two activations. Some settings did not converge or had too few telemetry observations. Some values are shown only in plots; table entries give standard deviations but the text does not report inferential tests.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out under the 60-row limit. Dataset-size-dependent peak curvature and cusp results were not included because the listed versions do not name those measurements.

untested.parts: Training classification error, including near-zero error with random or corrupted labels and its dependence on model size or training recipe.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and the effect of additional student neurons.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization and normalization exceptions.
Effects of alternative initializations on learning speed and trainable depth; initialization is held fixed.

The squared-loss wide-network catapult sequence; recovery versus divergence as a function of the initial stability threshold; divergence despite starting below that threshold. Full-gradient loss trajectories and long-time loss decline are not directly quantified in the supplied results. Failed tanh runs have no reported initial-threshold comparison.
Training-speed and learning-rate-tolerance comparisons with and without batch normalization, including Fixup.

missing.what: Condition-specific top-eigenvalue stability trajectories across the main series, including VGG-16-tanh and learning rates missing from the ratio rows. Record sustained near-threshold behavior separately from the pooled lower bound; VGG-16-tanh at η=0.0001 has only two telemetry observations.
AlexNet-ReLU at η=0.001 with 2, 3 and 5 classes shows near-threshold behavior in nc−1 eigendirections, with separation from the next eigenvalue.
Direct ρ1–ρ9 trajectories resolving entry into the edge of stability during the 2000-iteration AlexNet-ReLU run at η=0.001; R26 currently records only the accompanying gradient change.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for the listed versions. The record incorrectly treats the full-batch sharpness component of V5 as untested. Conversely, its projected-step measurements should not be treated as direct evidence of the full-gradient loss trajectory. Tanh nonconvergence at η=0.003 does not warrant a challenge or scope limitation without establishing the relevant stability-threshold condition.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, model size, early stopping and regularized recipes are not tested.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem, spurious-minimum frequency, or student-width comparison.
No depth comparison of plain and residual networks, and no tests of shortcuts, special initialization for plain tanh networks, or normalization-free residual networks.
No comparison of activation-matched and alternative initializations, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, or 10,000-layer convolutional networks. All reported experiments use Kaiming initialization.

The study uses non-stochastic gradient descent without momentum on CIFAR-10 with AlexNet and non-normalized VGG-16; it does not test the squared-loss wide-network recipe or full-batch sharpness hovering/divergence claims as phrased in the version.
No batch-normalization comparison, accuracy-speed measure, or learning-rate tolerance comparison.

rows.operation_detail: Measured the edge-of-stability ratio ρ9=η/η9* during non-stochastic gradient descent.
rows.measure: ρ9, lower bound on the top-subspace ratios ρi for i≤9
rows.note: The text gives this bound across all architectures at the lowest learning rate; this row identifies the AlexNet-ReLU condition.
rows.check: The numerical lower bound is correct, but does not by itself measure how closely sharpness hovers at the threshold. The observed state also relies on Sections 5.1 and 5.4 explicitly describing persistent near-threshold top eigenvalues.

rows.value: ρ10 never exceeds 0.246 at any point
rows.note: The text states this bound across all architectures at the lowest learning rate; the bulk ratio is below the edge of stability.
rows.check: ρ10 describes bulk curvature, not maximum sharpness. Its remaining below the threshold neither establishes nor contradicts V5.

rows.operation_detail: Measured the training gradient magnitude alongside the edge-of-stability ratio every 10 iterations.
rows.measure: Gradient magnitude ||gθ||2 as ρ1,...,ρ9 enter the edge of stability
rows.value: Gradient magnitude explodes at the same iteration the eigenvector enters the edge of stability
rows.note: The text describes simultaneous timing for the measured gradient magnitude and edge-of-stability entry.
rows.check: The timing statement matches Section 5.2, but gradient magnitude or concentration is not loss recovery or sharpness hovering. Figure 4's separate ρ1–ρ9 trajectories should be recorded directly for V5.

relationships.condition: Convergent full-batch AlexNet and non-normalized VGG-16 experiments on CIFAR-10 with ReLU or tanh across the reported learning rates
relationships.reason: R1, R3, R12 and R18, together with the missing Figure 1 and Figure 4 trajectories, support the sharpness-threshold component: top eigenvalues rise toward and remain near 2/η. This verdict uses the text and figures, not the projected-step loss rows.
relationships.display_finding: Top Hessian eigenvalues rose toward and remained near 2/η during convergent training.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
